rows.title: Monetary Policy
rows.figure: Fed Dec hike ~95% 25bp / ~5% 50bp (CME FedWatch via Hercules); ECB Dec ~90%; BoJ Dec ~84%; BoE Dec ~70–75%; BoC Dec ~44%; RBA minutes 6–3 on the November hike
rows.read: Firm US retail sales kept a December Fed hike near certain, and nothing overnight changed the picture elsewhere. Europe, Britain and Japan are still expected to hike, Canada and New Zealand look more likely to wait, and Australia's board is split. US rates still look set to rise fastest, which keeps favouring the dollar.

rows.title: Growth
rows.figure: US retail sales Oct +0.2% m/m (fcst +0.1%), control group +0.6% (fcst +0.4%), Sep +0.8% unrevised; Japan Q3 GDP −0.1% annualized; euro-area IP Sep +0.2% m/m
rows.read: US shoppers kept spending in October, with spending outside cars stronger than expected, so the US economy still looks firmer than most. Japan's economy shrank in the summer, euro-area factories are barely growing and China's demand is soft. That gap supports the dollar against the euro, yen and Aussie.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: UK regular pay 3.5% 3m/y (fcst 3.5%; prior 3.7%); NZ two-year inflation expectations 2.36% (Q3 2.34%); UK CPI Oct fcst 3.6%, Wed 1:00 AM CT
rows.read: UK pay growth cooled in line with forecasts, so UK inflation figures on Wednesday will matter more for the pound. New Zealand businesses' inflation expectations barely moved, giving its central bank no new reason to hike. US inflation is still well above the Fed's goal, which keeps up the pressure to raise rates.

rows.title: Risk Sentiment
rows.figure: Nasdaq −2.5%, Dow −739 points Monday; USD/JPY overnight low ~158.90; AUD/USD ~0.6722; NZD/USD ~0.5484
rows.read: Monday's sharp fall in US tech shares spread to Asia overnight and briefly lifted the yen. New Iranian drone attacks on Bahrain and tanker strikes in the Gulf added to the unease without sparking wider fear. The Aussie and kiwi, which track market mood, slipped to their lowest in months.

rows.title: Terms of Trade
rows.read: Oil fell further overnight on the supply-surplus outlook, then bounced as attacks on tankers kept coming. That keeps some support under the Canadian dollar. Gold stays near a 13-month low, which adds to the Aussie's troubles.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: CFTC report of Nov 10 (out late after Veterans Day): hedge funds for USD, GBP, AUD and gold; against EUR, NZD, CAD and CHF; slightly against JPY; real money disagrees on EUR, GBP and AUD
rows.read: The latest weekly figures show hedge funds leaning toward the dollar and the pound and against the euro, the kiwi and the Canadian dollar, with bets against the kiwi growing fastest. Big long-term investors take the other side on the euro, pound and Aussie. Where the two groups disagree, a surprise could set off a fast unwind.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.figure: US October deficit $404B, a record for the month; US 10-year ~5.14%
rows.read: Record US government borrowing keeps long-term US borrowing costs above 5%, and firm retail sales nudged them a little higher. Higher yields support the dollar for now, but a growing deficit is a worry if buyers start asking for more. France's debt troubles keep weighing on the euro.
